blocks.why: Bank forty minutes in the afternoon because I know I'll never fall asleep at 20:00 for an 06:10 report.
Lights out at 20:15 local to get anything useful in before the 03:35Z drive to the airport.
Second early in a row — straight to bed off the CDG turns, no evening at all.
Pay back the two short nights as soon as I'm through the door from ARN.
Normal night in my own bed — the ORD report isn't until 13:35Z so I can sleep to a civilised hour.
Top up before the Chicago sector because I'll be shutting the door at 01:05 body time.
Straight to bed on arrival at ORD and stay on London time — it's a one-night stop, no point flipping.
Two and a half hours mid-afternoon local to cover the all-night sector home.
Short sleep after the red-eye, then up again so I don't wreck tonight's proper sleep.
Long night to reset fully — the CDG/BCN day doesn't finish until 00:27 local.
An hour before report so the last BCN sector home isn't flown on fumes.
In bed as soon as I'm home from BCN, and no alarm — it's a day off.
Back onto a normal night to be square for the midday ARN turn.
Straight night's sleep, nothing on tomorrow.
Hold the normal pattern on days off rather than drifting late.
Full night before an easy afternoon DUB there-and-back.
Get up early on the day off deliberately, to start dragging my clock towards Monday's 05:05 report.
Nap in the middle of the day off so the ridiculous 19:30 bedtime tonight is survivable.
Bed at 19:30 local — the only way to get seven hours in before a four-sector day starting at 04:05Z.
Evening nap after the FRA doubles, kept short so I can still sleep tonight.
Sleep in as late as the body will allow — tomorrow night is the JFK red-eye.
Proper three-hour afternoon sleep before a 21:40 report; this is the nap that flies the aeroplane to New York.
Into bed at JFK the moment I'm in the room, while it's still night on my body clock.
Late-afternoon nap in New York to cover a 00:20Z report and another night crossing.
A few hours after landing, then force myself up — I need a real night before the Singapore sector.
Full night at home so I start the thirteen-hour SIN leg fresh.
Arrive Singapore breakfast time and sleep anyway — it's the middle of my night and I'm not flipping for one stop.
Sleep on London hours again — up at 13:30 Singapore, three hours clear of the 17:00 local report.
Everything I can get after the SIN arrival — under six hours, so I'll want bunk rest on the way in and I'm flagging this one.
Second short night running; straight in the door from FCO, straight to bed, alarm for the 07:00Z drive.
Nine and a half hours with no alarm to clear the debt from the last three days.
Afternoon top-up so I can go to bed at 19:30 for the 05:40 report.
Early night for the first of three consecutive dawn starts.
Nap straight off the FRA turn — tomorrow is a thirteen-hour day off a 05:05 report.
Bed at 19:30 again; this is the sleep that has to carry four sectors to FCO and BCN.
Six hours is all the roster leaves me between a 13-hour duty and an 04:25 report — asleep within twenty minutes of getting home.
Anchor sleep in the afternoon — this is my night's sleep, taken before the FCO night duty rather than after it.
Post-night-duty sleep, capped at lunchtime so I can get back on days for the sim.
Full night to flip back before an 08:00 sim — melatonin timing and a dark room matter here.
Sim done, month done — normal night.
Day off; keep the rhythm rather than sleeping the clock round.
Last night of the period, back on a normal London pattern for whatever October brings.

conflicts.statement: The '+1' day markers are hung on the local-time column but printed after the Zulu time as well, so 06:35/22:35Z+1 at SIN reads as either 22:35Z on the 18th or the 19th; the same happens with the 16SEP JFK report (20:20 local = 00:20Z on the 17th) and the 05SEP ORD arrival. I have resolved all of them by flight time — SIN arrival is 2026-09-18T22:35Z.
options: Cross-check the SIN, JFK and ORD dates against crew control's published UTC pairing before you plan around them
Ask ops to reissue the roster with fully dated Zulu times
Treat my UTC readings as the working set — every sector block time comes out sensible on them

conflicts.statement: 06SEP is printed OFF, but the ORD red-eye lands at 08:00Z and you are not off duty until 08:30Z that morning, so the 'day off' is really a post-night-flight recovery day.
options: Treat 06SEP as recovery, not leisure — no commitments before mid-afternoon
Ask whether the day off is meant to start at 08:30Z or at 00:00Z; it changes what protection it gives you
Take the split sleep I've planned (nap on landing, long night) rather than trying to stay awake all day

conflicts.statement: You are off duty at LHR at 00:20Z on 21SEP after a 15h20 duty home from Singapore across seven time zones, and report again at 10:20Z the same morning for a 12h11 four-sector day. That is 10h00 gate to gate; take 95 minutes each way off it and you have about 6h20 at home and under 6h in bed, at the wrong end of a body clock that is still somewhere over Asia.
options: Ask crew control to move the 21SEP report later or drop the FCO sector pair
Request a hotel at LHR for the night of the 20th/21st to buy back the 3h10 of commuting
Take maximum in-flight bunk rest on HY440 and treat it as the night's sleep
Log it as a fatigue report and consider calling unfit if the SIN sector runs late

conflicts.statement: Second short night in a row: off duty 22:31Z on the 21st, report 08:35Z on the 22nd — 10h04 minus commuting leaves roughly 6h50 at home, and you start that block already down from the Singapore night.
options: Ask for the 22SEP duty to be reduced from four sectors to two
Hotel at base again on the night of the 21st/22nd
Plan controlled rest on the DUB and CDG sectors with the other pilot
Fatigue report covering the 20th-22nd as a block, not as single days

conflicts.statement: 24SEP, 25SEP and 26SEP report at 04:40Z, 04:05Z and 03:25Z — three consecutive starts inside the window where sleep before duty is short and shallow, each one waking you deeper into the 02:00-06:00 body-time trough than the last.
options: Ask for one of the three to be moved to a later start
Accept the 19:30 local bedtimes I've planned and protect them absolutely — no evening commitments on 23rd, 24th or 25th
Blackout blinds and no caffeine after midday on those days
Flag the cumulative pattern to your fatigue safety group even if each day is individually legal

conflicts.statement: 25SEP is a 13h17 duty from an 04:05Z report ending at 17:22Z, and you report again at 03:25Z on the 26th. That is 10h03 rest; after 3h10 of commuting you get about 6h00 in bed, then fly four sectors starting at 04:25 local.
options: Ask crew control to break the 25/26 pairing — this is the worst single junction in the month
Hotel at LHR on the night of the 25th to convert commuting time into sleep
Pre-agree controlled rest on the DUB sectors on the 26th
Consider calling fatigued on the 26th if the 25th runs late at all

conflicts.statement: You come off duty at 13:22Z on the 26th having woken at 01:20Z, and report again at 23:25Z the same day for an FCO night duty that lands at 06:22Z — the whole sector sits in the 02:00-06:00 body-time window, on the back of a week of dawn starts.
options: Protect the 16:15-22:15 local anchor sleep on the 26th; it is the night's sleep, not a nap
Ask for the 26SEP day duty to be shortened or removed so the night duty starts from a rested state
Plan the caffeine for the FCO-LHR leg, not the outbound
Fatigue report the 26/27 double-duty day regardless of outcome

conflicts.statement: The simulator reports at 07:00Z on the 28th, about 24 hours after finishing a night duty at 06:52Z on the 27th — you have to flip from back-of-clock to a 06:00 local alarm with one night in between, and a check ride is not the place to be doing that.
options: Ask the training department to move the sim to the afternoon of the 28th or to the 29th
Cap the post-duty sleep on the 27th at early afternoon as planned so the night of the 27th/28th is genuinely restorative
Tell the trainer at brief that you flew a night duty 24 hours earlier
